summary: Comprehensive Astronaut Healthcare Monitoring and Digital Research Ecosystem
details:
ASTRA HEALTH & AQUA SIGNAL

Comprehensive Astronaut Healthcare Monitoring and Digital Research Ecosystem

Project Overview

ASTRA HEALTH is a research-oriented healthcare monitoring platform designed to explore the continuous assessment of astronaut health across multiple physiological systems during space missions.

The platform combines structured healthcare data management, biomarker analysis, statistical anomaly detection, predictive trend analysis, risk assessment, and decision-support capabilities within a unified software architecture.

Its healthcare reference catalogue covers 14 domains, including cardiovascular health, hematology, immune cell subsets, cytokines, inflammation, metabolic function, kidney and liver function, bone and muscle health, viral monitoring, vital signs, and radiation exposure.

The current prototype includes a synthetic astronaut simulation environment, a Python analytical backend, a FastAPI REST interface, a Streamlit dashboard, and SQLite-based persistence.

Core Capabilities

  • Multi-domain healthcare and biomarker data organization.
  • Astronaut-specific historical data and personal-baseline analysis.
  • Statistical anomaly detection using Robust Median Absolute Deviation.
  • Biomarker trend forecasting using linear regression.
  • Rule-based health-risk assessment and decision support.
  • Healthcare data exploration, alerts, history, and reporting.
  • API-based integration and research workflow management.

AQUA SIGNAL – Digital Research and Device Simulation

AQUA SIGNAL is a connected research-workflow simulator within the ecosystem. It demonstrates research-case creation, digital artifact generation, SHA-256 integrity verification, virtual device pairing, simulated data transfer, session-state management, and follow-up observations.

Its current implementation is software-only and does not control physical medical hardware or deliver therapeutic interventions.

Future Development

The planned evolution includes integration of real sensor and laboratory data, an LLM-based intelligence layer, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for scientific knowledge retrieval, improved device identity and firmware security, and validated astronaut-specific health reference models.

Mission

To develop an integrated research platform that supports the monitoring, analysis, prediction, and human-reviewed interpretation of astronaut healthcare information throughout space missions.
